events.title: François Grimaldi seizes the fortress of Monaco
events.description: Disguised as a Franciscan friar, the Genoese Guelph François Grimaldi talked his way into the Rock of Monaco and took it. His descendants, the House of Grimaldi, still rule the principality.
events.html: Disguised as a Franciscan friar, the Genoese Guelph François Grimaldi talked his way into the Rock of Monaco and took it. His descendants, the House of Grimaldi, still rule the principality.

events.title: Andrew Jackson defeats the British at New Orleans
events.description: Jackson's mixed force repulsed a British assault on New Orleans, inflicting some 2,000 casualties. Fought after the Treaty of Ghent was signed but before news arrived, it made Jackson a national hero.

events.title: Woodrow Wilson presents his Fourteen Points
events.description: Addressing Congress, President Wilson outlined a peace programme including open diplomacy, free seas, self-determination and a league of nations. It framed the armistice and the Paris Peace Conference.

events.title: Abdulaziz ibn Saud proclaimed King of the Hejaz
events.description: After conquering Mecca and Medina, the Sultan of Nejd was proclaimed King of the Hejaz in the Great Mosque of Mecca. In 1932 he merged his realms into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
events.html: After conquering Mecca and Medina, the Sultan of Nejd was proclaimed King of the Hejaz in the Great Mosque of Mecca. In 1932 he merged his realms into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

events.title: Britain introduces food rationing
events.description: Bacon, butter and sugar became the first foods rationed in wartime Britain. Rationing extended to most foods during the war and did not end entirely until 1954.
events.html: Bacon, butter and sugar became the first foods rationed in wartime Britain. Rationing extended to most foods during the war and did not end entirely until 1954.

events.title: Charles de Gaulle takes office as President of France
events.description: De Gaulle became the first President of the Fifth Republic, whose constitution greatly strengthened the executive. He governed France until 1969, ending the war in Algeria in 1962.
